title: Sinapelo jackfruit: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Sinapelo jackfruit: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Sinapelo jackfruit is a jackfruit variety from Felimon Sinapelo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Sinapelo is a registered jackfruit variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Jf 01. Felimon Sinapelo bred it. Its record notes a yield of 17 to 25 fruits/year.

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [jackfruit variety finder](/crop-varieties/jackfruit), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 17 to 25 fruits/year.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Sinapelo was about 8 years old and about 10 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 17 to 25 fruits/year. It bears every year, with fruit in March May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit jackfruit fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Sinapelo weighs about 8000 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is yellow orange and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 29.7 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 48.3 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is March May, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Sinapelo jackfruit

Pick a selection by flesh: firm and crisp for fresh eating and processing, or soft and sweet. Grafted trees of a named selection bear true. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Sinapelo?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
